challenges.name: map-lookup-and-container-choice-quiz
challenges.title: Predict the output: lookups that insert, and picking a container
challenges.description: Read each snippet the way the standard library runs it: which calls add a key, which only look, and which container fits the job.

questions.explanation: seats["CS103"] does not find CS103, so operator[] inserts it with int{} = 0 and returns a reference to that 0. 0 > 0 is false, so "CS103 open" is not printed - but the map now has 3 entries. contains() and find() only look: they never insert, so CS104 and CS105 are not added and nothing is printed for them. size is 3. at("CS106") does not insert either: for a missing key it throws std::out_of_range, and with GCC's standard library what() is "map::at". After the catch the size is still 3. "size 2 ... size 2" assumes operator[] only reads, as in Python or JavaScript - not in C++. "size 5 ... size 6" treats every lookup, and at(), as an insert. "CS103 open ... 0 ... size 4" would need the inserted value to be above 0 and at() to return a default value and insert it; it does neither. Nothing here fails to compile: the map is not const, so operator[] is allowed, and it is allowed for missing keys - that is exactly when it inserts.

options.text: size 2, then error: map::at, then size 2
size 3, then error: map::at, then size 3
size 5, then error: map::at, then size 6
CS103 open, then size 3, then 0, then size 4
It does not compile: seats["CS103"] is not allowed for a key that is missing

questions.question: The exam office ports its attendance tools to C++23. Which of these choices are correct? (Select all that apply.)
questions.explanation: std::map keeps its keys sorted (a balanced tree, O(log n) per lookup), so iterating it prints the class list in id order with no sort step. std::unordered_set is a hash set with average O(1) insert and lookup, which fits a "seen already?" check where order does not matter. The iteration order of std::unordered_map is unspecified: it depends on the hash function and the number of buckets, so it can change after more inserts or a rehash, or with another library version - in a GCC 15 run, the same five ids came out in a different order after rehash(64). A stable export needs std::map, or a copy that you sort. operator[] is a non-const member function because it may insert: calling it on a const std::map& does not compile (GCC: "passing ‘const std::map<...>’ as ‘this’ argument discards qualifiers"); use find(), contains() or at() instead. For counting, inserting 0 for a new key is exactly what you want, so ++counts[id] is the idiomatic way to count in either kind of map.

options.text: To print the class list sorted by student id with no separate sort step, keep it in a std::map<std::string, int>.
To check whether a card was already scanned in this session, with no order needed, use a std::unordered_set<std::string>.
Iterating the same std::unordered_map always gives the same order in one program, so the nightly CSV export can rely on it.
A report function that takes const std::map<std::string, int>& attendance can return attendance[id]: for an unknown id it returns 0 and leaves the map unchanged.
Counting check-ins per student with ++counts[id] is a correct use of operator[]: inserting 0 for a new id is what counting needs.

challenges.name: attendance-report
challenges.title: Write attendance_report(roster, checkins, queries)
challenges.description: The CS101 attendance report of Riverside Polytechnic, ported to C++23. The input is the class list, the card scans of the term as "<session> <student id>" and the ids the faculty office asks about. Count, for every student on the class list, the number of different sessions they attended (two scans in one session count once; scans by ids that are not on the class list are ignored). Answer each query with "<id>: <sessions>" or "<id>: unknown" without adding anyone to the class, then print the class list sorted by id as "<id>,<sessions>" (students with 0 sessions included) and finally "class size: <n>". The starter file has the full specification and an example.

tests.name: Every student is listed sorted by id, also with 0 sessions
Unknown ids are answered unknown and do not join the class
A card scanned twice in one session counts once
Scans by students of another class are ignored
Incident class: 8 students, double scans, foreign scans and repeated typo queries
